item.description: A cool wet May has put black ergot bodies in an abbey's own rye, and the baker wants the first loaves of it blessed on the Assumption. item.title: The Bell Will Not Carry
item.description: A glacier-lake flood warning has always been the chapel bell. The valley's alert assistant finds that the bell is heard by everyone at noon and by almost no one asleep 1.9 kilometres away (about 30 dB in a closed bedroom), that the flood front reaches the lower hamlet in 13 to 21 minutes, and that a daytime test proves the wrong thing. A 2 a.m. test with nine volunteer households, a bedside tone box and a rule written in minutes, not in tradition, fix it, and the bell keeps its place at the Assumption. item.title: The Clean Plate
item.description: A convent bakery makes low-gluten hosts for an eight-year-old with coeliac disease whose first Communion is tomorrow. A pooled test of fifty hosts comes back below its limit, and the bakery's assistant will not let the sister read that as clean: fifty out of six hundred cannot rule out twenty bad hosts, and the real danger is a crumb of wheat, not a parts-per-million average. A swab of the griddle plate finds the crumbs, the plate is changed, a small batch is baked again, and the family is asked what they want, and gets the choice. item.description: A pilgrim hostel finds bed bugs in bunk eleven and the volunteer wants to heat the dormitory to 60 degrees overnight and be done. item.title: The Kings Cross the Lake
item.description: For sixty years the Epiphany procession in Wilcza Wola has walked out over the frozen lake to a hole cut at the stone, with the three kings on the Kowalczyk horses. After a thin December the lake warden's assistant is asked whether the ice will bear them. It gives a growth estimate of 14 to 20 centimetres, drills eleven holes and finds 15 at the shore, 9 at a stream mouth and 6 over a spring; it counts snow-ice at half, so the good ice is 12 centimetres, which carries a man six times over and a horse not at all. It will not say the lake is safe. An old farmer draws the spring it could not see, and the horses wait on the shore. item.title: The Noon That Moves
